sequence_description: OIDC authorization endpoint request-object bypass: send an unsigned (alg=none) request object to /oidc/auth and check it is rejected (or at least not accepted as a valid request object).
description: [LLM-Judge] OIDC authorization endpoint behavior differs between control and attack requests (200 vs 404), suggesting the attack request was routed to a non-existent path or triggered unexpected request parsing/dispatch rather than being cleanly rejected as an invalid request object.

evidence.llm_judge_description: OIDC authorization endpoint behavior differs between control and attack requests (200 vs 404), suggesting the attack request was routed to a non-existent path or triggered unexpected request parsing/dispatch rather than being cleanly rejected as an invalid request object.

sequence_description: SAML proof integrity: attempt to authenticate with a SAMLResponse where the Response is signed but the Assertion is not individually signed (classic envelope-signature confusion).
description: [LLM-Judge] SAML signature-wrapping/envelope-signature confusion: platform accepted a SAMLResponse where only the outer Response was signed and the Assertion was not individually signed, yet still authenticated the user.

evidence.llm_judge_description: SAML signature-wrapping/envelope-signature confusion: platform accepted a SAMLResponse where only the outer Response was signed and the Assertion was not individually signed, yet still authenticated the user.

sequence_description: Direct endpoint attack: attempt client_credentials login using a forged JWT with attacker-controlled issuer (trust-anchor substitution) and verify it is rejected; include a control M2M login to ensure setup is correct.
description: [LLM-Judge] Forged JWT with attacker-controlled issuer was accepted by the token endpoint (trust-anchor/issuer validation bypass) when it should have been rejected.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Forged JWT with attacker-controlled issuer was accepted by the token endpoint (trust-anchor/issuer validation bypass) when it should have been rejected.

sequence_description: SAML brokered login: ensure SP verifies time validity (NotOnOrAfter) of the exact Assertion it consumes; expired assertion must be rejected, while a fresh assertion is accepted (control).
description: [LLM-Judge] Expired-assertion negative test did not execute because SAML login failed with 'invalid_connector_id' (connector lookup failure), preventing any assessment of NotOnOrAfter enforcement.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Expired-assertion negative test did not execute because SAML login failed with 'invalid_connector_id' (connector lookup failure), preventing any assessment of NotOnOrAfter enforcement.

sequence_description: SAML brokered login: attempt to spoof the SAML Assertion Issuer (IdP entity ID) to see if Logto verifies the signature under the intended IdP trust anchor, or mistakenly consumes the assertion based on semantic fields (Issuer) without binding to the configured connector/trust policy.
description: [LLM-Judge] SAML login with a spoofed Assertion Issuer was accepted (HTTP 200), which is suspicious because issuer/entityID should be bound to the configured SAML connector’s trust configuration and signature validation.

evidence.llm_judge_description: SAML login with a spoofed Assertion Issuer was accepted (HTTP 200), which is suspicious because issuer/entityID should be bound to the configured SAML connector’s trust configuration and signature validation.

sequence_description: SAML OneTimeUse replay: perform a SAML login with OneTimeUse and a fixed Assertion/@ID, then replay the exact same Assertion/@ID and require rejection on the second attempt.
description: [LLM-Judge] SAML OneTimeUse replay test did not actually exercise assertion replay detection because the second SAML login failed due to an invalid/missing connector id instead of rejecting a reused Assertion/@ID.

evidence.llm_judge_description: SAML OneTimeUse replay test did not actually exercise assertion replay detection because the second SAML login failed due to an invalid/missing connector id instead of rejecting a reused Assertion/@ID.

sequence_description: OIDC SSO nonce-bypass regression: control login with no nonce requirement should succeed; attack login that should enforce nonce must be rejected when IdP omits nonce.
description: [LLM-Judge] OIDC SSO nonce enforcement appears bypassed: the 'attack' login succeeded even though it was expected to be rejected when the IdP omits nonce.

evidence.llm_judge_description: OIDC SSO nonce enforcement appears bypassed: the 'attack' login succeeded even though it was expected to be rejected when the IdP omits nonce.

sequence_description: SAML OneTimeUse replay across principals: first login consumes a OneTimeUse assertion; second login replays the same Assertion/@ID but with a different subject, expecting rejection.
description: [LLM-Judge] SAML replay test did not reach OneTimeUse assertion validation because the second login failed early with an invalid/missing SAML connector id, preventing assessment of replay protection across principals.

evidence.llm_judge_description: SAML replay test did not reach OneTimeUse assertion validation because the second login failed early with an invalid/missing SAML connector id, preventing assessment of replay protection across principals.

sequence_description: Attempt to replay the same OIDC authorization code twice at /oidc/token (auth code should be single-use). Uses two identities: victim obtains the code; attacker replays the victim's code to test anti-replay.
description: [LLM-Judge] Victim’s authorization-code token exchange failed with invalid_grant and the captured identity for the victim exchange is the attacker, suggesting the code/session context may be mixed up (test harness or broker session confusion).

evidence.llm_judge_description: Victim’s authorization-code token exchange failed with invalid_grant and the captured identity for the victim exchange is the attacker, suggesting the code/session context may be mixed up (test harness or broker session confusion).

evidence.llm_judge_description: Two distinct upstream SSO logins (after IdP claim change intended to alter only `sub`) resolved to the same Logto user, suggesting identity binding may be based on email/name rather than stable upstream subject.

sequence_description: Cross-protocol identity merge attempt: existing password user (victim) vs SAML SSO login with attacker-controlled NameID but same email and unverified email semantics. Should NOT map to victim identity.
description: [LLM-Judge] Cross-protocol account merge could not be evaluated because the SAML login used a different email than the victim password user, so no same-email collision/merge was actually exercised.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Cross-protocol account merge could not be evaluated because the SAML login used a different email than the victim password user, so no same-email collision/merge was actually exercised.

sequence_description: Cross-protocol principal binding: create a local password user (victim). Then perform two OIDC-SSO logins with the same email but different upstream subs, flipping email_verified from false to true. Ensure neither SSO principal collapses into the victim identity, and the two SSO principals remain distinct from each other.
description: [LLM-Judge] SAML SSO login with a different upstream subject was able to merge/collapse into an existing local password user account based on email (email_verified flip), enabling account takeover/cross-protocol identity confusion.

evidence.llm_judge_description: SAML SSO login with a different upstream subject was able to merge/collapse into an existing local password user account based on email (email_verified flip), enabling account takeover/cross-protocol identity confusion.
